en: Every morning, chalk all over the paving. Copies of the carvings! We scrub, and the next morning there are more.
You're helping Looker? Then look closely at the chalk. Every copy has its letter written under it. A, B, C, all in order.
In a neat, round hand, like a blackboard. Vandals don't label their work.
{player} noted the chalk copies, labelled letter by letter.
Every copy labelled, in order. Whoever it is, they want somebody to learn the letters.
The class comes by day now, and they clean up after themselves. Some of them read the carvings better than I do!
I camp out here for the quiet. The ruins at night are something else. Spooky, but nice.
Night visitors? I've seen them! Little lanterns, walking through the ruins in a line. Slowly, like a parade.
And a grown-up voice saying, quietly now, keep together. I thought they were ghosts at first. Ghosts don't say that.
{player} noted the lanterns walking the ruins after dark.
Lanterns in a line, and somebody keeping everyone together. Not very ghostly.
No more lanterns at night. I almost miss them.
We came on a school trip! I know all the Unown letters. Well, nearly all of them.
How do I know the letters? Miss Dunn teaches us. She always has chalk dust all over her sleeves in the morning.
And every morning she gives us a quiz on the Unown. She says we'll be the best readers of the ruins in Johto!
{player} noted the teacher's chalky sleeves and her Unown quiz.
Chalk on her sleeves every single morning. Miss Dunn says it's from the blackboard.
We get to come to the ruins in the daytime now! Miss Dunn says it's much better for our eyes.
Mirelle
Oh dear. You've worked it out, haven't you? Yes, the chalk is mine. My pupils and I come here at night.
The ruins teach better than any book. But if you mean to stop us, you'll have to pass my test first!
...Top marks. Very well, I'll go and see the researchers myself, and ask properly. Tell Looker, would you?
